item.title: Hindustan Zinc Q2 net profit surges 142% to ₹6,412 cr on record Ebitda
item.description: Higher zinc and silver prices, increased production and lower zinc production costs boosted Hindustan Zinc's quarterly earnings, while revenue from operations rose 76.5% ...
item.dc:creator: Saket Kumar
item.content:encoded: Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL) reported a 142 per cent surge in net profit at ₹6,412 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27) from ₹2,649 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) more than doubled to a record ₹9,285 crore, supported by higher metal prices, increased production and lower zinc production costs. The Vedanta group firm reported a 77 per cent increase in revenue from operations to ₹15,093 crore during the quarter, compared with ₹8,549 crore a year earlier.   Zinc production cost, excluding royalty, declined 29 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to $703 per tonne. The company attributed the reduction to better mined grades, higher metal production, increased consumption of renewable power and higher by-product realisations. These gains were partly offset by lower domestic coal usage and higher input commodity prices. Hindustan Zinc reported record second quarter mined metal production of 271,000 tonnes, up 5 per cent Y-o-Y, while refined metal production rose 7 per cent to a record 264,000 tonnes for the quarter. Silver production increased 20 per cent to 173 tonnes, contributing to profitability. Revenue from zinc sales rose 54 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹8,224 crore, while silver sales revenue surged 141 per cent to ₹4,111 crore. Lead sales revenue increased 35 per cent to ₹1,130 crore. For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations rose 77 per cent to ₹28,840 crore. Ebitda increased 108 per cent to ₹17,359 crore, while net profit climbed 143 per cent to ₹11,881 crore. As of September 30, the company had gross investments and cash of ₹17,439 crore and outstanding borrowings of ₹6,171 crore. Separately, Hindustan Zinc said it had secured a letter of intent for the Gundlupet Rare Earth Element and Yttrium Block in Karnataka, advancing its diversification into critical minerals.

item.title: Jio Platforms' anchor book draws record ₹2.5 trillion in bids ahead of IPO
item.description: Jio Platforms is set to raise up to $3.2 billion at a valuation of $108.3 billion in what will be India's biggest ever IPO ...
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: Jio Platforms allotted shares worth Rs 8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at the top end of its price band, after institutional demand for the offering exceeded Rs 2.5 trillion, more than 30 times the amount available in the anchor book, according to a stock exchange filing and people familiar with the matter. The allotment of 7.24 crore shares at Rs 1,119 apiece comes two days before the initial public offering opens for public subscription on Wednesday. The strong demand underscores institutional investor interest in what is expected to be India's largest IPO, although the extent to which it translates into broader public demand will become clearer once the offer opens. Life Insurance Corporation of India received the largest allocation, worth Rs 499.98 crore, accounting for 6.17 per cent of the anchor portion. New World Fund Inc was allotted shares worth Rs 486.27 crore, followed by the Government of Singapore at Rs 340.93 crore, SBI Focused Fund at Rs 315 crore and BNP Paribas Financial Markets - ODI at Rs 303.25 crore. Domestic mutual funds received 2.489 crore shares worth Rs 2,784.96 crore, representing 34.34 per cent of the anchor book, through 95 schemes across 25 fund houses. Life insurers and pension funds received 97.4 lakh shares worth Rs 1,089.95 crore, or 13.44 per cent of the total. Both categories exceeded the allocations reserved for them under the red herring prospectus dated October 14, which earmarked 33.33 per cent of the anchor portion for mutual funds and 6.67 per cent for insurers and pension funds. Global investment firms participating in the anchor book include BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson. Sovereign and public investment institutions include the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and the Monetary Authority of Singapore, alongside other long-term institutional investors. Some large overseas and domestic institutions bid for allocations worth USD 750 million to more than USD 1 billion each, people familiar with the matter said. Jio Platforms is seeking to raise about Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, at a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece. The offering values the company at around USD 108 billion, according to the offer documents. The IPO will open on October 21 and close on October 23. Proceeds will partly be used to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, with the remainder earmarked for general corporate purposes. Reliance Industries Ltd, controlled by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will retain a majority stake in Jio Platforms after the listing. Jio Platforms has grown into one of the world's largest mobile operators by subscriber numbers since Reliance entered the telecom market a decade ago. The business has expanded beyond mobile connectivity into broadband, digital entertainment, cloud and enterprise services, making it the central part of Reliance's push into India's digital economy. The company had 533.3 million subscribers as of June 2026 and carried nearly 60 per cent of India's data traffic, according to reported company figures. The listing will give public-market investors direct exposure to a business that has so far operated as a subsidiary of Reliance Industries. Its scale and the breadth of institutional participation make the offering a closely watched test of investor appetite for large Indian equity issuances. The anchor book, which allows institutional investors to receive shares before the public subscription period, represents about 27% of the total IPO. Demand exceeding 30 times the anchor allocation, alongside subscriptions at the top of the price band, provides an early indication of institutional appetite for the offering. However, strong anchor demand does not guarantee similar enthusiasm from retail investors or ensure gains after listing. Investors will weigh Jio's subscriber base and opportunities in digital services against competitive pressures, regulatory risks, capital requirements and its ability to translate scale into sustained revenue and profit growth, analysts said. The offering also provides a measure of the Indian market's capacity to absorb a transaction of this size, with domestic mutual funds, insurers and pension funds accounting for nearly half of the anchor allocation. The public subscription will offer a clearer indication of whether that institutional confidence extends across the wider investor base

item.title: US bans Chinese AI DeepSeek from civilian government agency IT systems
item.description: The US has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek AI products and related services from IT systems, citing national security risks and concerns over potential data transfers to China.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Technology / Artificial Intelligence / US bans Chinese AI DeepSeek from civilian government agency IT systems

US bans Chinese AI DeepSeek from civilian government agency IT systems The US has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek AI products and related services from IT systems, citing national security risks and concerns over potential data transfers to China.

The US has ordered civilian federal agencies to remove Chinese AI model DeepSeek and related services from government IT systems, citing national security risks and concerns over potential data transfers to China. (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 12:12 AM IST

Listen to This Article

The US Homeland Security Department is ordering the removal of DeepSeek products and third-party services using the Chinese AI model from US civilian agency IT systems, according to a notice published Monday.   The department is also banning acquisition of DeepSeek products and third-party services developed using DeepSeek by US civilian government agencies. DHS said DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees or vendors."   DHS also said use of DeepSeek by government agencies "could produce actionable intelligence on US persons and/or government agencies. The models themselves may contain malware or other security vulnerabilities."

In a July memo made public Monday, DHS told federal agencies to monitor flows of traffic in and out of government websites to address potential risks from DeepSeek.   Previously, several US agencies, including the Department of Commerce and the Navy, have banned the use of DeepSeek on government devices. Multiple states including New York, Tennessee, and Virginia have taken similar steps. Also Read

The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately comment.   The Trump administration has taken a series of steps to crack down on Chinese tech companies.   The Federal Communications Commission will vote on October 29 to bar all Chinese labs from testing electronic devices such as smartphones, cameras and computers for use in the US. Last year, 82% of US electronics were tested in China.

In December, the FCC banned import of all new models of Chinese drones and also banned imports of new models of Chinese-made consumer routers, the boxes connecting computers, phones and smart devices to the internet.   In July, the FCC voted to bar sales of devices in the US that contain key hardware from Chinese companies deemed to be national security risks and has proposed to prohibit US telecommunications carriers from interconnecting with Chinese telecom firms deemed national security risks

item.title: China's growth accelerates to 4.5% in third quarter, beats expectations
item.description: Beijing has leaned heavily on exports for growth this year, but that engine faces growing pressure as domestic demand remains weak and trade tensions with the European Union escalate ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's economic growth rebounded to 4.5% year-on-year in the third quarter, beating expectations and easing the pressure on policymakers for delivering more aggressive stimulus measures to meet the annual target. The third-quarter gross domestic product growth rate, released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Monday, beat the forecast for 4.4% growth in a Reuters poll, and improved from the more-than-three-year low of 4.3% in the April-to-June period. Beijing has leaned heavily on exports for growth this year, but that engine faces growing pressure as domestic demand remains weak and trade tensions with the European Union escalate. China's strategy of redirecting credit and resources from property towards high-tech industries has created a two-speed economy, where strong factory output and exports mask weak consumption and private investment. For January-September, the economy grew 4.6%, within the range of the government's annual growth target of 4.5%-5.0%. On a quarterly basis, the economy expanded 1.2% in the third quarter, surpassing expectation for a 1.1% rise and accelerating from 0.9% in April-June. China's trade surplus widened more than expected in September as exports surged, keeping the country on track to surpass last year's record surplus of $1.2 trillion and likely intensifying trade tensions with major partners. A deal with the EU to rein in Chinese hybrid-vehicle shipments could weigh on the booming auto trade. Beijing has recently expanded support for home buyers, unveiled measures to steer cheaper credit into sectors including infrastructure and technology and allocated 550 billion yuan ($82.28 billion) in unused government debt quotas to ease local governments' financial strain and expand infrastructure investment. Authorities also stepped up fiscal support, including expanding loan interest subsidies for small private firms and consumers and tapping an 800 billion yuan policy-based financing tool to spur infrastructure investment. Still, infrastructure investment shrank 4.2%. Fixed-asset investment declined 7.2% in the first nine months, dropping at the same pace as in January-to-August period. Retail sales grew 1.1% in September, improving from the 0.4% rise in August and compared with an expected 0.6% rise. It marked the quickest growth since March. Property investment fell 20.6% in the first nine months in September. Policymakers refrained from releasing large-scale stimulus, as strong goods exports, aided by a global AI-fuelled tech boom, should help the country to reach its annual growth target. Industrial output expanded 5.5% in September, accelerating from the 5.2% growth in August and was in line with expectations. It marked the quickest growth in six months.  China mulls overnight rate as main policy benchmark China’s central bank is considering switching its main policy rate to the overnight reverse repurchase rate, in a shift aimed at improving the transmission of monetary policy to support the economy. The overnight repo rate would replace the seven-day reverse repo rate, which has served as the main policy benchmark since 2024. People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng said the change is part of efforts to refine the bank’s control of short-term interest rates, according to a readout of Pan’s speech by the central bank.  “Currently, the interbank overnight repo rate has effectively become the target rate for the PBOC’s monetary policy,” Pan said.
